dialogueEntries.text: Ash takes you to a quiet spot by a river.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Thanks for coming out here with me.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: Of course. Everyone knows the first thing you should do with someone is to let them take you to a secluded spot in the woods.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Hah. Yeah, of course. I swear I won't do anything to you, though.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: Yeah, yeah, I trust you, don't worry.
This world is far too perfect for me to get kidnapped right now...

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: It's nice here. Thanks. It beats going home.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: That's odd. Most people can't wait to go home after their first day of school.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: And yet, here we are. We must be fools.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Yeah... I like home, but to be honest, sometimes my parents can be a little overbearing.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: That's why I come out here every once in awhile. It's quiet... nice to get out, you know?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: So yeah, welcome to my little corner. I don't usually take people here until I get to know them better. You must be special.'

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: Special, huh?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: So your guitar. Why'd you bring it today?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: I was always planning to come out here afterschool. I usually take my guitar.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: It's relaxing just being surrounded by nature and the sound of the strings, you know?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: Yeah... the silence helps out here, too.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: Today was... honestly one of the best days I've had in awhile. But I'm still waiting for something to happen. It's like I don't trust it.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: And it feels like my head is screwed on backwards. Like I just woke up from a long dream... or maybe like I'm still in one.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: I don't know if it's me... or everybody else that's acting crazy...

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Maybe if you play something it'll help?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: No, no, it's okay. You can play something though.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: No, I shouldn't, you should. It'll help you!

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: What'll help me is if you play me a song now.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Hmm... you have to give me a good reason why.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: Because it'll help me stop thinking about how crazy everything feels right now?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: ..Hmph... point heard...

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: I don't often have audiences... but since you asked...
He starts up a simple arpeggio. He looks a little nervous, but then unexpectedly, starts to sing.
It's a song you recognize. You know the harmony to it.
Of course you do. You start to sing along.
It's peaceful. Your voices compliment each other.
For a moment you get lost into the music. And then it ends as quickly as it started.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Wow. You didn't tell me you sang.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: You didn't, either.
He's starting intently. Does he want to-?
He's starting intently. Does he want to-?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: There's just no way.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: What do you mean?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: You! All of this! There's just no way in hell.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Ayla, speak to me calmly. Did I do something wrong?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: Ash. What's your type?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: My... type? Romantically?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: What else?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: I guess... artistically inclined people? And... alternative dressing, too, if I'm honest.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: So kind of like me?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: ...yeah?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: What about your stance on kids? Do you want any in the future?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: ...No, well, at least not biological ones? I would consider fostering or adopting?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: But Ayla, what does this have to do with-

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: What about your stance on politics?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Ayla, can you tell me-

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: Answer me first.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: ...Well... I think everyone should be politically active. Ignorance will always catch up to someone.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: I knew it.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Knew what?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: You're too PERFECT, Ash.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: ...I mean... thanks?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: You misunderstand. I mean, what are the chances of meeting the ideal, infuriatingly perfect potential partner on my first day of high school?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: On a day where everything has been nothing less than perfect, this is no coincidence.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: I don't understand, Ayla. What are you saying?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: Are you even real? I mean, REALLY. Are you THINKING right now? Is everything just DESIGNED for me?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: I-

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: Where did the grief go? The bullying? How do I know that you- or ANYONE else is real?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Of course we're real-

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: And then there's me. I don't even think I'm SUPPOSED to be here right now. The last thing I remember is-

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Ayla.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: You are alive. I promise you.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: ...am I? What is this place? Is it some kind of purgatory...?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Does it matter? This feels real. It's all you need. You don't have to suffer, anymore.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: You've been slowly suffocating for years. But here you can finally breathe.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Does that sound so bad?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Does that sound so bad?

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: I can't do that. I need to know the truth or drive myself crazy trying.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: Goodbye, Ash. I'm going home. To my REAL home.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Good luck, Ayla.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Good luck, Ayla.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: No... it doesn't sound bad...

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ash
dialogueEntries.text: Then don't worry about it. Just live.

dialogueEntries.speaker: Ayla
dialogueEntries.text: I... okay..
You haven't kissed anyone before this. It's short. It's nice.
You two talk for hours, learning about each other. You lay on his shoulder.
It feels like it was expertly molded to fit your cheekbone. But maybe that's not a bad thing.
